messages:
alex: seeing noisy scale-downs on the gpu-pool in us-west-2 — cluster-autoscaler is evicting GPU pods even when we have PDBs. Any ideas?

maria: ugh. which pods are being evicted? are they StatefulSets or using local emptyDir/hostPath?

alex: mostly model-serving deployments (ReplicaSets) and a few jobs with local tmp scratch. PDBs exist but scale down still goes through sometimes.

jeff: CA shouldn't delete pods that would violate a PDB. Could be that the pods are marked non-evictable (local storage) or the eviction API failing and CA resorting to forceDelete. Check controller-manager and CA logs.

alex: here's a snippet from k8s-bot when it tried to drain node gpu-02: 
```
I0805 12:03:21.123456 1 drain.go:345] Evicting pod model-a-5f7d... failed: eviction API not supported by apiserver: unable to evict pod as it would violate the poddisruptionbudget 
W0805 12:03:22.123456 1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:512] Force deleting pod model-a-5f7d due to node removal
```

maria: that second line is key — force delete happened. Why did controller fall back? maybe eviction API errors intermittently or kube-apiserver rejected for another reason (rbac/quotas).

infra-oncall: we had an apiserver hickup around that time (throttling), will check metrics. But we should also mitigate: make GPU pods explicitly evictable where possible and tune CA scaleDownDelay/UnneededTime to avoid spurts.

jeff: agree. two practical paths: 1) make pods friendly to eviction (avoid local storage or add annotation cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true when it's ok), 2) use PDBs + priorityClass to control which pods are protected. But be careful: giving everything high priority prevents CA from reclaiming nodes -> cost spike.

maria: here's a minimal PDB we use for the realtime model replicas: 
```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: realtime-models-pdb
spec:
  maxUnavailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: realtime-model
```
Keep maxUnavailable small so updates can proceed but CA will respect it.

alex: what about priorityClass? example?

jeff: priorityClass example: 
```yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: critical-gpu
value: 100000
globalDefault: false
description: "Protect critical model-serving pods from eviction by kubelet preemption."
```
Use sparingly for genuinely critical pods.

infra-oncall: another pattern: set a lower priority for batch/spot inference so CA can evict those first. Combine with node taints for spot vs reserved GPUs.

maria: also verify pod has tolerations and nodeSelector so CA understands they're node-pool-bound. CA sometimes struggles if pods are tightly binpacked and fragmentation prevents safe move. Consider increasing binpack fragmentation by allowing smaller replica counts across nodes.

alex: any safe drain checklist we can standardize for gpu nodepools?

jeff: short checklist: 
- Ensure critical replicas have PDBs that reflect true availability needs (minAvailable/maxUnavailable).
- Use priorityClass for only the small set of non-negotiable pods.
- Mark clients that can be moved with cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true.
- Avoid local persistent hostPath volumes; use PVCs or emptyDirs that can be recreated.
- Tune CA: scaleDownUnneededTime and scaleDownUnreadyTime to avoid preemptive removals during short spikes.
- Add a pre-drain hook (operator or job) to gracefully checkpoint and remove local scratch before eviction.

maria: plus, on k8s side: set the eviction API retry/backoff to be more permissive and monitor apiserver error rates; when we saw the forceDelete it correlated with apiserver throttling.

infra-oncall: I'll open a short runbook PR with the checklist and add an alert when CA falls back to forceDelete for pods on node drain.

alex: thanks — also want to discuss cost impact: some teams want CA to be aggressive to save $ but we need guardrails for GPU workloads.

jeff: suggestion: create two node pools: reserved-gpu (for priorityClass critical) with min nodes to guarantee capacity, and preemptible/spot-gpu pool for low-priority with aggressive scale-down. CA can prefer removing spot pool first with expander config and Taints.

maria: +1. Also add a metric: "gpu_nodes_evicted_with_force_delete" so we can quantify how often apiserver issues cause unsafe drains.

alex: ill take the runbook items and we can iterate. ping me if infra-oncall finds apiserver issue. :thumbsup:

k8s-bot: created issue #2142: "runbook: gpu node safe-drain checklist + alert on force deletes" assigned to infra-oncall.
